records.name: Love Now Media
records.summary: A media and storytelling group whose Love Lab hosts public events on art, dialogue and AI education, and whose Poet's Press publishes poetry and commentary.
records.what_you_do: Reserve a spot at a Love Lab event or a Poet's Press writing workshop through the reserve links on the site. Poets can send work through the Poet's Press submission form, and anyone can join the mailing list or subscribe to the magazine.

schedule.text: Events are posted one at a time, each with its own reserve link.

cost.text: Some events are ticketed. The homepage does not show prices, so check each event listing.

first_step.how: Pick a Love Lab event or Poet's Press workshop on lovenowmedia.com and use its reserve link, or join the mailing list to hear about the next one.
first_step.basis: Events and workshops are open to the public and each has a clear reserve link, but the site does not describe what a visit is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical event. Each event has its own listing, so read it for the time, place and price before you reserve. Some events are paid tickets.
first_visit_tips: Check each listing for the price before you reserve, since some events are ticketed

records.notes: Event reservations and tickets run through Eventbrite. We recorded only what the group's own site shows and did not open the Eventbrite listings, so no event dates, times or prices are recorded. The Oct 2, 2026 homepage post is the newest dated evidence.

records.name: Lutheran Settlement House Qigong Class
records.summary: A weekly qigong class for adults 55 and up at the Lutheran Settlement House in Fishtown, with slow movement, breathing, and meditation.
records.what_you_do: Move through qigong postures and breathing exercises with others your age, at any skill level.

cost.text: No fee is listed on the page. Call the office to confirm.

first_step.how: Come to a Thursday class at the Fishtown office. No registration is needed.
first_step.basis: The page says the class is open to all levels and abilities for ages 55 and up, and that you can simply come without signing up.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each class lasts one hour and moves through qigong postures, slow whole-body movement and breathing, with a short meditation. You join other adults 55 and older. The page does not list a fee, so ask the office about cost before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 426-8610 to ask about the cost and which entrance to use

records.notes: The page lists the next class on Thursday, October 8, 2026. It has no wheelchair, parking or transit details, so access is left out. The site had no fee or entrance details beyond tier 1.

records.name: Mothers In Charge
records.summary: A Philadelphia violence prevention group that supports families who have lost someone to violence. It runs a monthly community breakfast, a welcome group for newly bereaved families, and a reentry dinner.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly community breakfast, join the welcome group for bereaved families, or ask about volunteering.

schedule.text: Community breakfast on the first Saturday of each month, 11 am to 1 pm. A welcome group for newly bereaved families meets monthly on a Tuesday, and a reentry dinner meets monthly on the third Wednesday.

first_step.how: Email info@mothersincharge.org with the subject 'First Saturday Breakfast RSVP' to save a seat at the breakfast, or call 215-228-1718 about the welcome group.
first_step.basis: The page says all are welcome at the breakfast and lists a welcome group for newly bereaved families, with a clear RSVP email and phone line.
first_step.what_to_expect: The first Saturday breakfast runs 11 am to 1 pm at the office and is free. The page says all are welcome. The page does not describe the welcome group in detail, so call to ask what a first meeting is like.
first_visit_tips: Send your RSVP ahead of the Saturday so a seat is held for you
Call 215-228-1718 if you want to know more before you come

records.notes: The breakfast is listed as first Saturday monthly, but a June post on the site calls it quarterly, so confirm before you go. The welcome group page says first Tuesday, yet its listed date was a third Tuesday. The office address reads Suite 301 on the page, while the map link shows Suite 703. The site describes no volunteer roles, requirements or background checks. Chapters in San Francisco, Los Angeles and Kansas City are out of area and not recorded.

records.name: Nicetown CDC
records.summary: A community development group in Nicetown that runs a yearly summer festival with concerts and a Land Care program for parks and gardens. The City lists it as the Friends group for Nicetown Park, but its website does not mention the park.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at the yearly Giveback Community Festival through the sign-up link on the site, or call the office about Land Care. Residents can act as stewards who look after vacant land on their blocks.

schedule.text: A yearly summer festival with concerts, held over two days in August.

cost.text: The site does not say whether the festival charges admission.

first_step.how: Start the festival volunteer sign-up from the link on nicetowncdc.org, or call (215) 324-9772 to ask about the Land Care program.
first_step.basis: The site has a volunteer sign-up and a phone line, but it does not say how a first time volunteer starts or what volunteers do on the day.
first_step.what_to_expect: The festival is a summer event with concerts and food and merchandise vendors. The site does not list volunteer shift times, what volunteers do, or whether the concerts cost money. Call the office to ask before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Call the office first to ask about shifts and the admission price
The office is on the third floor at 4414 Germantown Ave, Suite A

records.notes: The volunteer sign-up link goes to a login page on a third-party site (Drexel), so a person may need to create a profile there; it was not used. The homepage calls the festival the 24th annual, while a 2023 news item calls it the 21st. The Land Care page lists no days, times, or volunteer roles, and no accessibility details appear on the site. The festival dates (Aug 7 and 8, 2026) are the newest dated evidence.

records.name: Northern Living Center
records.summary: A senior community center on North Franklin Street with group exercise, games, crafts, music, outings, and one-on-one help with Medicare, Social Security, and other benefits.
records.what_you_do: Join group exercise and wellness activities, play games or billiards, take part in arts and crafts, music or workshops, or book a benefits counseling appointment.

schedule.text: Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 4 pm; Thursday until 7 pm; Saturdays by scheduled days only.

cost.text: No membership or program fee is listed. The page invites tax-deductible donations.

first_step.how: Call (215) 978-1300 or complete the senior application online, then schedule a tour to meet staff and see the activities.
first_step.basis: Older adults are welcome and the site gives a clear way in: call, apply online, or book a tour. A membership application is needed before joining programs.
first_step.what_to_expect: A tour lets you meet staff and learn about the activities and services before you start. Programs cover exercise, games, crafts, music, outings and education, and staff can help with benefits questions. The page does not list fees or age rules, so ask when you call.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 978-1300 to confirm age requirements and book a tour
Ask about parking, transit and wheelchair access when you call, since the site does not cover them

records.notes: The site links a senior application and an activity calendar, but gives no accessibility, parking, transit or fee details. Saturdays run by schedule only, so call before a Saturday visit. The age rule for members is not stated on the page.

records.name: PA CareerLink Philadelphia
records.summary: The city's public job center network, funded through federal and state workforce programs. It offers free help with resumes, interviews and job searches, plus workshops and hiring events at centers and libraries.
records.what_you_do: Book a career appointment, attend a free workshop, or come to a hiring event and meet employers.

schedule.text: Free workshops on resumes, interviews, job search, LinkedIn and networking are held on weekdays at centers and libraries. Sign up through the workshops calendar.

locations.label: North, Northwest and West Philadelphia centers, Suburban Station, and several Free Library branches

cost.text: Career services, workshops and the job search site are free. Workshops require a PA.gov account to register.

first_step.how: Call 1-833-750-5627, or use the appointment link on the contact page to book a career appointment. To attend a workshop, register through the workshops calendar.
first_step.basis: The site lists a Welcome to PA CareerLink orientation workshop for first visits, plus a phone line and online appointment booking, all at no cost.
first_step.what_to_expect: Start with the Welcome to PA CareerLink orientation, which runs about an hour at a library or center. Staff then help with resumes, interviews, LinkedIn and job searches, and many sessions are offered in Spanish. Workshops are free but need a PA.gov account to sign up.
first_visit_tips: Create your PA.gov account before you register, since the site says workshops need one
Ask for Spanish-language sessions or other help when you book, since aids are available on request
Confirm the time on the event page, because some listings show unusual end times

access.notes: The centers are wheelchair accessible, according to the site. Auxiliary aids and services are available on request for people with disabilities. Many sessions run in Spanish, and some are virtual through the PHL Career Portal.

records.notes: The workshop calendar runs September 28 to October 31, 2026 and lists more than 100 sessions, so the record describes the types of sessions rather than listing dates. The Awareness Day job fair on October 14 is at Community College of Philadelphia and needs its own registration. Some hiring events on the homepage are cited from Facebook posts, which were not read and are not recorded.

records.name: Panorama Toastmasters
records.summary: A Philadelphia Toastmasters club that meets in person to practice public speaking and leadership. Guests can visit for free, as often as they like, before deciding to join.
records.what_you_do: Practice short speeches and impromptu talks, take on meeting roles, and get feedback from other members.

schedule.text: First and third Wednesdays, 7:00 to 8:45 pm, at Project Joy Studio. Second Saturdays, 1:00 to 2:45 pm, at the Donatucci library branch.

locations.label: Thomas F. Donatucci, Sr. Library (Saturday meetings)

cost.text: Guests attend free. Dues are about $15 a month, billed every six months, plus a one-time $40 fee for new members.

first_step.how: Come to a meeting as a guest, free and as often as you like. To ask questions first, use the contact form on the club's website.
first_step.basis: Guests are explicitly welcome and can attend free as often as they like before joining. The site also asks newcomers to arrive a few minutes early.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings usually start on time, so arrive a few minutes early to meet members. The club learns by doing, and members build skills at their own pace in a social, friendly room with a mix of people. Street parking is on most nearby streets, but read the signs.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes early so you can meet members before the meeting starts
Bring nothing special, since guests need not bring anything
Read the parking signs on nearby streets before you park

records.notes: Membership applications go through a Toastmasters application link linked from the club's contact area. The site gives no accessibility or transit details and does not describe meeting roles or speech formats in detail.

leads_only.name: Furtick Farms
leads_only.note: Community garden behind the Nicetown CDC community center, named on the Land Care page as a Nicetown CDC project. Not checked as a separate group.

notes: All seven groups were fetched on their own sites, using 11 of up to 60 fetches and no WebSearch. Nicetown CDC's volunteer link goes to a third-party login page; it was not used. Mothers In Charge chapters in San Francisco, Los Angeles and Kansas City are out of area. Within budget: nothing ran out.
